A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FTM/FLA research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures, equations and proofs, support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original LIBERO/LIBERO-V experiments, adaptation ablations, visual-embedding analysis and real-world Franka manipulation outcomes.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds robustness cases, expanded adaptation-rank results and additional training-step comparisons.

M1.justification: The core FTM affine transformation and FLA low-rank updates remain unchanged. However, v1 Section 11 explicitly projects FTM prompt tokens through an MLP, whereas v2 Section 12 omits that projection while Figure 4 still depicts it. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a procedural change or revised documentation.

E1.justification: V2 Section 7.5 adds a real-world scenario where the target object is manually displaced during execution, extending evaluation beyond static visual perturbations. The LIBERO/LIBERO-V coverage and original five Franka tasks are retained.

E2.justification: The training-step comparison expands from π0.5 LoRA versus FLA in v1 Figure 10 to include π0 LoRA/FLA and a π0.5 full-fine-tuning baseline in v2 Figure 12. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 Table 8 expands the rank configurations to 8, 16, 32 and 64 across OpenVLA-OFT, π0 and π0.5. Figure 12 extends the training-step evaluation to 2,500 steps from 2,000. The manual target-disturbance test adds a testing procedure; the established benchmark protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of imperfect demonstrations and dynamic target disturbances in Sections 7.4–7.5, substantially expands rank sensitivity across architectures in Table 8, and broadens training-stability comparisons in Figure 12. V1 already contained narrower rank/training-step ablations and the retained embedding-alignment analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing 50-trials-per-task statement is retained, and the added tables and training curves continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial results through Table 8, expanded training curves and real-world robustness cases, including 89.0% for OpenVLA-OFT with rank-8 FLA and a separately reported 90.7% under imperfect demonstrations. Tables 1 and 3 change FTM's viewpoint entry from 87.2% to 87.1%. The headline FLA results remain 90.8% for viewpoints and 94.8% for LIBERO-V.

T1.justification: The mathematical method formulations, three assumptions, three theorems, proofs and combined error bound are retained. V1 Section 7 becomes v2 Section 8; the model and flow-matching derivations likewise remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction changes the spatial/physical decomposition from an adopted recent paradigm to a proposed conceptual framework, modestly revising contribution attribution. The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the central bottleneck, lightweight adaptation and generalization claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets imperfect-demonstration resilience as evidence of visual realignment and dynamic-object recovery as a benefit of closed-loop control. It also adds interpretations about faster convergence, resistance to overfitting and hyperparameter robustness. These extend the earlier discussion without revising its central explanation.

D1.justification: V2 removes the explicit MLP-projection detail from FTM's training description. Figure 1 also changes the VLM size label from 2B to 2.6B, although the appendix retains its 2B backbone description. Hardware, preprocessing, optimizer settings and Table 7 hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds eight references, including SpatialVLA, VLM4VLA and RADAR, and explicitly connects its conceptual decomposition to prior discussions of spatial reasoning. The related-work organization and broad positioning around targeted visual adaptation remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized grammar and terminology corrections, revises the introductory attribution, adds acknowledgments and expands appendix discussion. The main-text real-world summary is removed while its substantive coverage remains in the appendix. Most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, moves the original real-world rollout figure into the appendix, adds Figures 8–9 and Table 8, and replaces the two-series training plot with an expanded five-series Figure 12. These substantially expand and reorganize the visual evidence; the embedding and viewpoint plots are retained with new numbering.

improvement.justification: The expanded rank/backbone comparisons, full-fine-tuning comparator and real-world stress cases provide useful additional empirical support. The gain is limited by sparse evaluation details for the new robustness results and unresolved FTM implementation wording. Some new claims of consistently superior convergence also exceed what Figure 12 shows, but the added evidence provides a modest net improvement.
